text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000092 bills 99215 far above expectation, mostly on low-complexity patients, yet every sampled 99215 chart documents high MDM, so the record is in tension.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The billing pattern points toward upcoding: the excess 99215 share is concentrated on patients with 0–1 chronic conditions, and those cases include simple acute complaints. Examples are a 21-year-old with a UTI code (C0048721) and a 30-year-old with an upper respiratory infection (C0048722). Against that, none of the 7 documented 99215 claims fell below the billed level. There is also no cloning signal on the data-reviewed check, so the paper record currently supports the billed levels, which is why this is not called upcoding. Seven charts is a thin base, and high MDM with 32–42 minutes for a routine URI or UTI is clinically surprising, so whether the notes reflect real complexity is the central ambiguity. A reviewer should first read the full notes for the documented low-complexity 99215s (C0048721, C0048722, C0048758) to see whether the stated problems, data and risk elements are specific to the visit or templated. The next step is to request records for more of the undocumented low-complexity 99215s, such as C0048652, C0048728 and C0048739, and to look at the heavy 99214 volume as well."}
